Ritu Project — Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 Cohort (Local/Early)

Author

Tianqi Ouyang

Published

April 9, 2026

Ritu cohort — Local/Early stage only. This page repeats the Jiaxuan carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 analysis on the subset of patients with tumor_stage == "Local/Early", leaving N = 142 patients. tumor_stage is dropped from Table 1 and from every adjuster set because it is constant within this cohort.

steroids is dropped from the adjuster sets on every page. On this page it was already excluded because all 142 patients in the subgroup received steroids, making the variable constant and collinear with the intercept; together with an emptied cancer_type_cat_7 “GI” level (cleared by droplevels() after the cohort filter) it made the design matrix rank-deficient and cmprsk::crr failed regardless of event count. steroids is retained as a descriptive row in Table 1.

Only the long-horizon kidney outcomes are modelled on this page. AKI within 1 year and the CKD composite are carried through Fine-Gray competing-risk models in Section 5, with death at any time as the competing event. The 90-day adverse-event, hospitalization and 90-day-death models this page used to carry have been removed; those outcomes are still derived in Data Management and remain in the saved master, they are simply no longer modelled. Read both models with their event counts in view — 12 AKI and 7 CKD-composite events in 142 patients against ~20 covariate degrees of freedom, so both are over-parameterised. See RITU_PROJECT.md.

# Output directory for downloadable Word tables
docx_dir <- "docs/tables/auc3"
dir.create(docx_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Output directory for editable PowerPoint copies of every figure. A knitr
# plot hook (defined below) saves last_plot() to docs/pptx/auc3/<label>.pptx
# and appends a download link after the figure in the rendered HTML.
dir.create("docs/pptx/auc3", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
pptx_dir <- normalizePath("docs/pptx/auc3", mustWork = TRUE)
pptx_rel_prefix <- "../pptx/auc3/"

.pptx_written <- new.env()
.pptx_pair    <- new.env()

.save_pptx <- function(p, path) {
  tryCatch({
    doc <- officer::read_pptx()
    doc <- officer::add_slide(doc, layout = "Title and Content",
                              master = "Office Theme")
    doc <- officer::ph_with(doc, rvg::dml(ggobj = p),
                            location = officer::ph_location_type(type = "body"))
    print(doc, target = path)
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.process = function(filename) {
  label <- knitr::opts_current$get("label")
  if (is.null(label)) return(filename)
  pair <- .pptx_pair[[label]]
  if (!is.null(pair) && inherits(pair$default, "ggplot") && inherits(pair$fine, "ggplot")) {
    p1 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
    p2 <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    ok1 <- .save_pptx(pair$default, p1)
    ok2 <- .save_pptx(pair$fine,    p2)
    rels <- c(if (ok1) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx"),
              if (ok2) paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, "_10pct.pptx"))
    if (length(rels)) .pptx_written[[label]] <- rels
    return(filename)
  }
  p <- tryCatch(ggplot2::last_plot(), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(p) || !inherits(p, "ggplot")) return(filename)
  pptx_path <- file.path(pptx_dir, paste0(label, ".pptx"))
  if (.save_pptx(p, pptx_path)) {
    .pptx_written[[label]] <- paste0(pptx_rel_prefix, label, ".pptx")
  }
  filename
})

local({
  default_chunk_hook <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("chunk")
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(chunk = function(x, options) {
    out <- default_chunk_hook(x, options)
    label <- options$label
    if (!is.null(label) && !is.null(.pptx_written[[label]])) {
      rel <- .pptx_written[[label]]
      if (length(rel) == 2) {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download top plot as PowerPoint</a> · <a href="%s" download>📊 Download bottom (10 %% ticks)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1], rel[2])
      } else {
        link <- sprintf(
          '\n\n<p style="margin-top:-0.5em;font-size:0.9em;"><a href="%s" download>📊 Download as PowerPoint (editable)</a></p>\n\n',
          rel[1])
      }
      out <- paste0(out, link)
    }
    out
  })
})

# --- Sparse-outcome guard (Ritu cohort) --------------------------------------
# Restricting to Local/Early disease leaves several outcomes with very few
# events (90-day death = 2; thrombocytopenia grade 3 and the individual
# hospitalization reasons are in the single digits). A model that cannot be
# estimated raises an error, which would abort the entire render, so every
# table / row / figure helper is wrapped below. On success the output is exactly
# what the Jiaxuan version produces; on failure a short note is emitted in place
# of the table or figure. No model specification is changed.
.wrap_tbl <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e) knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "\n::: {.callout-warning}\n",
    "## Model not estimable in this cohort\n\n",
    "Too few events among the ", nrow(dat), " Local/Early patients to fit ",
    "this model with the full adjuster set.\n\n",
    "Error: `", conditionMessage(e), "`\n:::\n")))
}
.wrap_row <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(time_var, status_var, label, ...) tryCatch(
    f(time_var, status_var, label, ...),
    error = function(e) {
      ev <- tryCatch(
        sum(as.character(dat[[status_var]]) == "1", na.rm = TRUE),
        error = function(e2) NA_integer_)
      tibble::tibble(
        Outcome = label, Model = "not estimable",
        N = NA_integer_, `Excluded (missing cov.)` = NA_integer_,
        Events = as.integer(ev),
        `(sub)HR (95% CI)` = "not estimable", `p-value` = "\u2014")
    })
}
.wrap_plot <- function(f) {
  force(f)
  function(...) tryCatch(f(...), error = function(e)
    ggplot2::ggplot() +
      ggplot2::annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, size = 3.4, lineheight = 1.3,
        label = paste0("Model not estimable in this cohort\n",
                       "(too few events among the ", nrow(dat),
                       " Local/Early patients)\n\n",
                       strwrap(conditionMessage(e), width = 60,
                               prefix = "\n", initial = ""))) +
      ggplot2::theme_void())
}

# Table 1 via tableone. Factor-like columns (factor / character / logical and
# indicator columns of 0/1) are summarised as n (%); every other numeric column
# as median [IQR], except the variables named in `normal_vars` (mean (SD)).
# Categorical variables with any observed cell < 5 get Fisher's exact test.
tableone_mat <- function(d, strata = NULL, normal_vars = "age") {
  d     <- as.data.frame(d)
  vars  <- setdiff(names(d), strata)
  is_fl <- vapply(d[vars], function(x)
    is.factor(x) || is.character(x) || is.logical(x) ||
      (is.numeric(x) && all(stats::na.omit(unique(x)) %in% c(0, 1))),
    logical(1))
  fct_vars  <- vars[is_fl]
  cont_vars <- vars[!is_fl]

  if (is.null(strata)) {
    tab   <- tableone::CreateTableOne(vars = vars, data = d,
                                      factorVars = fct_vars, test = FALSE)
    small <- NULL
  } else {
    tab <- tableone::CreateTableOne(
      vars = vars, strata = strata, data = d, factorVars = fct_vars,
      addOverall = TRUE, test = TRUE, argsExact = list(workspace = 2 * 10^7))
    small <- fct_vars[vapply(fct_vars, function(v)
      any(table(d[[v]], d[[strata]]) < 5), logical(1))]
    if (!length(small)) small <- NULL
  }

  mat <- print(tab, nonnormal = setdiff(cont_vars, normal_vars), exact = small,
               showAllLevels = TRUE, missing = TRUE, printToggle = FALSE,
               noSpaces = TRUE, quote = FALSE)
  tibble::as_tibble(cbind(Characteristic = rownames(mat), mat),
                    .name_repair = "unique")
}

save_tbl_docx <- function(tbl, docx_name) {
  ft <- gtsummary::as_flex_table(tbl)
  flextable::save_as_docx(ft, path = file.path(docx_dir,
                                               paste0(docx_name, ".docx")))
  invisible(tbl)
}

# Load the Local/Early cohort, then keep only carboplatin patients
dat <- readRDS("ritu_final_master.rds") %>%
  filter(platin_group == "Carboplatin", carbo_AUC >= 3) %>%
  # Ritu: clear factor levels left empty by the cohort filter above,
  # so the model matrices stay full rank (cmp_status_* excluded --
  # their 0/1/2 coding is relied on downstream).
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

# Create eGFR ratio: CKD-EPI Cr-Cys (unindexed) / Cockcroft-Gault
# Also create per-10 mL/min rescaled versions of cockcroft and CKD-EPI for
# reporting (HRs per 1 mL/min are clinically uninterpretable; convention in
# nephro-onc is per 10 mL/min — bio_agent confirmed). Adjusters keep raw scale.
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    # Capped versions (for dose discrepancy calculations)
    cockcroft_cap125 = pmin(cockcroft, 125),
    # ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex_cap125 already exists in data
    # Ratio uses UNCAPPED eGFR
    egfr_ratio    = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / cockcroft,
    egfr_ratio_per10 = -egfr_ratio * 10,  # per 0.1-unit *decrease* reporting scale
    egfr_discrepancy = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft,
    # per-10-mL/min DECLINE reporting scale for eGFR discrepancy: HR for this
    # variable reads as the multiplicative change in subHR per 10 mL/min lower
    # discrepancy (i.e., when CKD-EPI Cr-Cys is 10 mL/min farther below CG).
    egfr_disc_per10dec = -egfr_discrepancy / 10,
    # Sensitivity-analysis eGFR ratio (Section 16):
    # numerator = CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C only (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed)
    # denominator = CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine only (baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed)
    # per10 below is the per-0.1 DECLINE reporting scale.
    egfr_ratio_sens       = baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_ratio_sens_per10 = -egfr_ratio_sens * 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR (new primary exposure):
    # egfr_diff_pct = 100 * (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys unindexed - Cockcroft-Gault) / Cockcroft-Gault
    # egfr_diff_pct_per10: HR reads as multiplicative change per 10 percentage-point DECLINE.
    egfr_diff_pct         = 100 * (ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex - cockcroft) / cockcroft,
    egfr_diff_pct_per10   = -egfr_diff_pct / 10,
    # Percent-difference eGFR for sensitivity analysis:
    # numerator - denominator = CKD-EPI 2012 CysC - CKD-EPI 2021 Cr, both unindexed.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens        = 100 * (baseline_cys_c_egfr_unindexed - baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed) / baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed,
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10  = -egfr_diff_pct_sens / 10,
    # Binary form of the same exposure: 1 when the cystatin C eGFR sits more
    # than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR. Reference level is ">= -10%".
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat    = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10, "< -10%", ">= -10%"),
      levels = c(">= -10%", "< -10%")),
    # Stricter cut at -30 %: a much smaller, more clearly discordant group.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30  = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -30, "< -30%", ">= -30%"),
      levels = c(">= -30%", "< -30%")),
    # Intermediate cut, between the primary -10 % and the stricter -30 %.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20  = factor(
      ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < -20, "< -20%", ">= -20%"),
      levels = c(">= -20%", "< -20%")),
    # Quartiles of the same continuous exposure. ntile() gives 1 to the most
    # negative quartile; Q4 (least discordant) is set as the reference level.
    egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4     = factor(
      dplyr::ntile(egfr_diff_pct_sens, 4), levels = 4:1,
      labels = c("Q4 (least discordant)", "Q3", "Q2", "Q1 (most discordant)")),
    # "Survivor": still in follow-up beyond one year.
    survivor_365              = days_last_follow_up > 365,
    # Dose discrepancy uses CAPPED eGFR (already computed in ritu_data.qmd)
    dose_discrep_per25increase = dose_discrepancy / 25,
    abs_dose_discrep = abs(dose_discrepancy),
    abs_dose_discrep_cat = cut(abs_dose_discrep,
      breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100, Inf),
      labels = c("<25", "25-49.99", "50-74.99", "75-99.99", ">=100"),
      right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
    # Binary exposure for adjusted CIF curves (Section 14): 1 if patient was
    # over-dosed by 25 mg or more (actual - predicted >= 25), else 0.
    dose_discrep_ge25 = as.integer(dose_discrepancy >= 25),
    # Signed dose discrepancy = actual - predicted; 10 bins symmetric around 0.
    signed_dose_discrep_cat = cut(dose_discrepancy,
      breaks = c(-Inf, -100, -75, -50, -25, 0, 25, 50, 75, 100, Inf),
      labels = c("<=-100", "-99.99 to -75", "-74.99 to -50",
                 "-49.99 to -25", "-24.99 to 0",
                 "0 to 24.99", "25 to 49.99", "50 to 74.99",
                 "75 to 99.99", ">=100"),
      right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE),
    cockcroft_per10 = cockcroft / 10,
    ckd_epi_per10   = ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex / 10
  )

cat("Carboplatin AUC >= 3 cohort N =", nrow(dat), "\n")
Carboplatin AUC >= 3 cohort N = 142

2 Actual vs Predicted Dose (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

Code 
dose_long <- dat %>%
  select(record_id, carbo_dose_redcap, carbo_dose_cre_cys) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(carbo_dose_redcap, carbo_dose_cre_cys),
    names_to = "dose_type", values_to = "dose_mg"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(dose_mg)) %>%
  mutate(dose_type = case_match(dose_type,
    "carbo_dose_redcap"  ~ "Actual (REDCap)",
    "carbo_dose_cre_cys" ~ "Predicted (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys)"
  ))

ggplot(dose_long, aes(x = dose_mg, fill = dose_type)) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = 0.5, bins = 40, position = "identity", color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Actual (REDCap)" = "#E31A1C",
                                "Predicted (CKD-EPI Cr-Cys)" = "#1F78B4")) +
  labs(title = "Carboplatin Dose Distribution (AUC ≥ 3)",
       x = "Dose (mg)", y = "Number of Patients", fill = "Dose Type") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

2.2 Signed Dose Discrepancy Distribution

Smooth kernel density estimate of the signed dose discrepancy (actual − predicted, CKD-EPI Cr-Cys). The area under the curve is shaded by sign — negative (under-dosed region) on one side, positive on the other.

Code 
dose_vals <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(dose_discrepancy)) %>%
  pull(dose_discrepancy)

dens <- density(dose_vals, n = 512)
y_at_zero <- approx(dens$x, dens$y, xout = 0)$y

dens_df <- tibble(x = dens$x, y = dens$y) %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(x = 0, y = y_at_zero)) %>%
  arrange(x)

neg_part <- dens_df %>% filter(x <= 0) %>% mutate(side = "neg")
pos_part <- dens_df %>% filter(x >= 0) %>% mutate(side = "pos")
plot_df  <- bind_rows(neg_part, pos_part)

ggplot() +
  geom_area(data = plot_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = side), alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = dens_df, aes(x = x, y = y), linewidth = 0.6, color = "black") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 25, linetype = "dotted", color = "grey30") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"),
                    guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-250, 250), ylim = c(0, 0.010)) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Signed Dose Discrepancy (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)",
       x = "Dose Discrepancy (mg) = Actual dose – Predicted dose",
       y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

3 Table 1: Baseline Characteristics (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

Code 
t1 <- dat %>%
  # Show the numeric KDIGO stage as a labelled factor for Table 1. get_ckd_stage()
  # collapses G3a/G3b into a single stage 3, unlike ckd_stage_cre / ckd_stage_cre_cys.
  mutate(ckd_stage_baseline = droplevels(
           factor(ckd_stage_baseline, levels = 1:5,
                  labels = c("G1 (>=90)", "G2 (60-89)", "G3 (30-59)",
                             "G4 (15-29)", "G5 (<15)")))) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    age, age_cat, sex, race, ethnicity, cancer_type_cat_7,
    carbo_AUC, carbo_AUC_cat,
    ici, Bevacizumab, Paclitaxel, Pemetrexed, Doxorubicin, Etoposide,
    Gemcitabine, Pertuzumab, Trastuzumab, Docetaxel, other_chemo, Administered_alone,
    hiv_rpdr, thyroid, smoking, steroids, esrd_kt,
    cci, score, ecog_score, bmi, bmi_cat,
    pre_HGB_45days, pre_PLT_45days, pre_ALB_45days, pre_CRE_45days,
    baseline_cys_c, baseline_cre, cr_cys,
    baseline_cre_egfr, baseline_cys_c_egfr,
    ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys, ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex,
    ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys,
    cockcroft, egfr_ratio,
    # Long-horizon kidney variables (Sections 5.16-5.19 of ritu_data.qmd).
    # eGFR_CRE_baseline / ckd_stage_baseline are baseline; last_cre_days is
    # creatinine follow-up length; the rest are outcomes over that full window,
    # NOT censored at 90 days like every other outcome in this project.
    eGFR_CRE_baseline, ckd_stage_baseline, last_cre_days,
    aki, aki_any, ckd_incidence, ckd_incidence_any, ckd_progression,
    eskd_defination_1, esrd_kt_after_ici, eskd_composite, ckd_composite,
    # Delta eGFR vs baseline at fixed marks (Section 5.16b). Negative =
    # decline. Closest creatinine within +/- 45 days of each mark.
    delta_egfr_d90, delta_egfr_d180, delta_egfr_d365,
    delta_egfr_pct_d90, delta_egfr_pct_d180, delta_egfr_pct_d365
  ) %>%
  tableone_mat()

cap_t1 <- sprintf(paste0(
  "Table 1. Baseline characteristics, N = %d. Continuous variables are ",
  "median [IQR] except age, which is mean (SD); categorical variables are ",
  "n (%%). Missing is the percent missing in the cohort."), nrow(dat))

flextable::flextable(t1) |>

3.1 Follow-up time (days from baseline to last known status)

Two alternative definitions of follow-up time shown side-by-side:

  • A — Raw days: unrestricted calendar follow-up (median dominated by patients who kept returning for years).
  • B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days: restricts to patients whose last-known contact was within 1 year of baseline.
Code 
followup_summary <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(record_id, days_last_follow_up) %>%
  tidyr::drop_na(days_last_follow_up)

fmt_med_iqr <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, 0.25), quantile(x, 0.75))
}

fu_row <- function(label, v) {
  tibble::tibble(
    Interpretation                  = label,
    N                               = length(v),
    `Median [IQR] follow-up (days)` = fmt_med_iqr(v)
  )
}

v <- followup_summary$days_last_follow_up
followup_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fu_row("A — Raw days",             v),
  fu_row("B — Raw days, ≤ 365 days", v[v <= 365])
)

flextable::flextable(followup_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption("Follow-up time from baseline to last known status (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 cohort). Two alternative definitions.") |>
  flextable::autofit()

3.2 Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)

Ported from the ICI-CKD project and built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of Data Management. Creatinine for these comes from the Ritu_project RPDR pull (Oct 2026).

None of these are censored at 90 days. A qualifying CKD episode has to be sustained for ≥ 90 days, so they run over the full length of RPDR creatinine follow-up. aki is restricted to events within 1 year. This section reports all of them descriptively; aki and ckd_composite are the two that are modelled — see the Fine-Gray section below. The rest are descriptive only.

Definitions as of the latest revision. aki is now restricted to events within 1 year of baseline (aki_any keeps the unrestricted count for reference and is not modelled). ckd_incidence uses a > 25 % eGFR drop; ckd_incidence_any drops the percent requirement entirely; ckd_progression now additionally requires a > 30 % further drop, where it previously counted any patient who was simply below 60 before and after — which flagged stable CKD as progression and is why that count fell sharply.

aki is also not the same variable as AKI_g2_90days / AKI_kdigo_90days: it compares each creatinine against the patient’s own preceding 90-day median (or 2-day low) rather than against a fixed pre-baseline value. The cross-tabulation below shows how far the two diverge.

📄 Download Word table

Code 
.kid_row <- function(flag, time_var, label) {
  n <- sum(dat[[flag]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  tt <- if (!is.null(time_var) && time_var %in% names(dat))
          dat[[time_var]][dat[[flag]] == 1] else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(dat)),
    `Median days to event (IQR)` = if (n > 0 && any(!is.na(tt)))
        sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(tt, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(tt, .25, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(tt, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
      else "-"
  )
}

kidney_lt <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .kid_row("aki",               "aki_days",                    "AKI within 1 year (serial creatinine)"),
  .kid_row("aki_any",           "aki_days_any",                "AKI at any time (reference only, not modelled)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence",     "time_to_ckd_incidence",       "CKD incidence (>25% eGFR drop to <60, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_incidence_any", "time_to_ckd_incidence_any",   "CKD incidence any (>=60 to <60, sustained >=90d, no % drop)"),
  .kid_row("ckd_progression",   "time_to_ckd_progression",     "CKD progression (<60 at baseline, further >30% drop, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("eskd_defination_1", NULL,                          "ESKD (eGFR <10, sustained >=90d)"),
  .kid_row("esrd_kt_after_ici", NULL,                          "ESRD / kidney transplant after baseline"),
  .kid_row("eskd_composite",    "time_to_eskd_composite",      "ESKD composite"),
  .kid_row("ckd_composite",     "time_to_ckd_composite",       "CKD composite (incidence + progression + ESKD composite)")
)

ft_kid <- flextable::flextable(kidney_lt) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(
    "Long-horizon kidney outcomes (N = %d). Not censored at 90 days.", nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()

3.3 Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs Baseline at 90 / 180 / 365 Days

Change in creatinine eGFR from eGFR_CRE_baseline, using the creatinine closest to each mark and taking it only when it falls within ± 45 days of that mark. Days run from baseline_sample_date. Built in Section 5.16b of Data Management.

Negative means decline. delta_egfr_d90 is eGFR at day 90 minus eGFR at baseline, so a fall in kidney function is a negative number — the opposite sign to pct_drop in the data-management pipeline.

The ± 45-day window matches the window used for every other baseline lab in this pipeline (pre_CRE_45days), and it is the widest window that stops the 90-day and 180-day marks drawing on the same measurement. It costs coverage at the later marks — the n column below shows how much.

📄 Download Word table

Code 
dgfr_marks <- c(90, 180, 365)

dgfr_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(dgfr_marks, function(mk) {
  d  <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_d", mk)]]
  dp <- dat[[paste0("delta_egfr_pct_d", mk)]]
  dy <- dat[[paste0("cre_day_d", mk)]]
  g  <- dat[[paste0("eGFR_CRE_d", mk)]]
  ok <- !is.na(d)
  q3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
         median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
  tibble::tibble(
    Mark = paste0("Day ", mk),
    n = sum(ok),
    `% with a value in window` = round(100 * sum(ok) / nrow(dat), 1),
    `Actual day` = sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]",
      median(dy[ok]), quantile(dy[ok], .25), quantile(dy[ok], .75)),
    `eGFR at mark` = q3(g[ok]),
    `Delta eGFR` = q3(d[ok]),
    `Delta eGFR (%)` = q3(dp[ok])
  )
})

ft_dgfr <- flextable::flextable(dgfr_tbl) |>
  flextable::set_caption(sprintf(paste0(
    "Delta eGFR (creatinine) vs baseline, N = %d. eGFR in mL/min/1.73m², ",
    "median [IQR] throughout. Negative = decline from baseline."), nrow(dat))) |>
  flextable::autofit()
flextable::save_as_docx(ft_dgfr, path = file.path(docx_dir, "sec3_3_delta_egfr.docx"))

.iqr <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return("—")
  sprintf("%.0f [%.0f, %.0f]", median(x), quantile(x, .25), quantile(x, .75))
}

why_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(0:3, function(k) {
  i <- .k == k
  tibble::tibble(
    `Marks covered` = paste0(k, " of 3"),
    n = sum(i),
    `% of cohort` = round(100 * sum(i) / nrow(dat), 1),
    `No post-baseline creatinine at all` = sum(i & dat$n_cre_post == 0),
    `Post-baseline creatinines, median [IQR]` = .iqr(dat$n_cre_post[i]),
    `Last creatinine, day, median [IQR]` = .iqr(dat$last_cre_days[i])
  )
})

4.2 eGFR Difference (sens) distribution

Signed eGFR difference (sens) = 100 × (CKD-EPI 2012 cystatin C − CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine) / CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine, both unindexed. Concordance sits at 0 %. Red bins are the negative side — cystatin C below creatinine, the muscle-wasting direction. The dotted line at − 30 % marks the strictest of the three cuts used for the binary exposures further down.

Code 
diffsens_hist <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_diff_pct_sens)) %>%
  mutate(side = ifelse(egfr_diff_pct_sens < 0, "neg", "pos"))

ggplot(diffsens_hist, aes(x = egfr_diff_pct_sens, fill = side)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(count) / sum(after_stat(count)) * 100),
                 binwidth = 2, boundary = 0, color = "black", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -30, linetype = "dotted", color = "#1F78B4", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(neg = "#E31A1C", pos = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of eGFR Difference (sens): 100 × (CysC − Cr) / Cr",
       subtitle = sprintf(paste0(
                          "Median %.1f %% of %d patients\n",
                          "Below -10 %%: %d (%.1f %%)   |   below -20 %%: %d (%.1f %%)",
                          "   |   below -30 %%: %d (%.1f %%)"),
                          median(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens),
                          nrow(diffsens_hist),
                          sum(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -10),

                          sum(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -20),

                          sum(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -30),
                          100 * mean(diffsens_hist$egfr_diff_pct_sens < -30)),

3.5 CKD Stage Reclassification — Creatinine vs Creatinine + Cystatin C

Every patient carries two KDIGO G-stages, both built in Data Management: ckd_stage_cre from baseline_cre_egfr (CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine) and ckd_stage_cre_cys from ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys (CKD-EPI creatinine + cystatin C). Both are indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²), so the two stagings sit on the same scale and the move between them is read directly.

Code 
stg <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(ckd_stage_cre), !is.na(ckd_stage_cre_cys)) %>%
  mutate(across(c(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys), droplevels))

ct <- table(stg$ckd_stage_cre, stg$ckd_stage_cre_cys)
knitr::kable(cbind(`Creatinine stage` = rownames(ct), as.data.frame.matrix(ct)),
  row.names = FALSE, caption = sprintf(paste0(
    "CKD stage by creatinine eGFR (rows) against creatinine + cystatin C eGFR ",
    "(columns), N = %d. The diagonal is unchanged; right of it the cystatin C ",
    "stage is worse, left of it better."), nrow(stg)))

recl <- stg %>%
  summarise(N = n(),
    `Worse stage`  = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) > as.integer(ckd_stage_cre)),
    `Unchanged`    = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) == as.integer(ckd_stage_cre)),
    `Better stage` = sum(as.integer(ckd_stage_cre_cys) < as.integer(ckd_stage_cre))) %>%
  mutate(across(c(`Worse stage`, Unchanged, `Better stage`),
                ~sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", .x, 100 * .x / N)))

                "G3a (45-59)" = "#EF6C00", "G3b (30-44)" = "#C62828",
                "G4 (15-29)" = "#6A1B9A", "G5 (<15)" = "#37474F")

.sk  <- stg %>% count(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, name = "n")
.N   <- sum(.sk$n)
.gap <- 0.055 * .N

# Node stacks: each stage a box, height proportional to n, separated by a gap.
.nodes <- function(col) .sk %>%
  group_by(stage = .data[[col]]) %>% summarise(tot = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(stage) %>%
  mutate(ntop = lag(cumsum(tot), default = 0) + .gap * (row_number() - 1),
         nbot = ntop + tot)
.ln <- .nodes("ckd_stage_cre"); .rn <- .nodes("ckd_stage_cre_cys")

.left <- .sk %>% arrange(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys) %>%
  group_by(ckd_stage_cre) %>%
  mutate(l0 = lag(cumsum(n), default = 0), l1 = cumsum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  left_join(.ln %>% select(ckd_stage_cre = stage, b = ntop), by = "ckd_stage_cre") %>%
  mutate(l0 = l0 + b, l1 = l1 + b)
.right <- .sk %>% arrange(ckd_stage_cre_cys, ckd_stage_cre) %>%
  group_by(ckd_stage_cre_cys) %>%
  mutate(r0 = lag(cumsum(n), default = 0), r1 = cumsum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  left_join(.rn %>% select(ckd_stage_cre_cys = stage, b = ntop),
            by = "ckd_stage_cre_cys") %>%
  mutate(r0 = r0 + b, r1 = r1 + b)

.fl <- .left %>% select(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, n, l0, l1) %>%
  left_join(.right %>% select(ckd_stage_cre, ckd_stage_cre_cys, r0, r1),
            by = c("ckd_stage_cre", "ckd_stage_cre_cys")) %>%
  mutate(flow = row_number(), pct = 100 * n / .N)

.xlb <- 0.07; .xle <- 0.22; .xrb <- 0.78; .xre <- 0.93
.tt <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 70); .ease <- 0.5 - 0.5 * cos(pi * .tt)

# One polygon per flow: out along its top edge on a cosine ease, back along
# the bottom. Tinted by the source stage so each origin stays traceable.
.rib <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  list(.fl$flow, .fl$l0, .fl$l1, .fl$r0, .fl$r1, as.character(.fl$ckd_stage_cre)),
  function(id, l0, l1, r0, r1, src) tibble::tibble(
    flow = id, Stage = src,
    x = c(.xle + (.xrb - .xle) * .tt, .xle + (.xrb - .xle) * rev(.tt)),
    y = c(l0 + (r0 - l0) * .ease, rev(l1 + (r1 - l1) * .ease))))

# Labels sit inside the box when it is tall enough, otherwise just outside it.
.nd <- dplyr::bind_rows(.ln %>% mutate(xmin = .xlb, xmax = .xle),
                        .rn %>% mutate(xmin = .xrb, xmax = .xre)) %>%
  mutate(big = tot >= 0.07 * .N,
         lab = ifelse(big, sprintf("%s\n%d (%.0f%%)", stage, tot, 100 * tot / .N),
                           sprintf("%s  %d (%.0f%%)", stage, tot, 100 * tot / .N)),
         tx = ifelse(big, (xmin + xmax) / 2,
                     ifelse(xmin < 0.5, xmin - 0.012, xmax + 0.012)),
         hj = ifelse(big, 0.5, ifelse(xmin < 0.5, 1, 0)))

.fll <- .fl %>% filter(pct >= 2.5) %>%
  mutate(lx = .xle + 0.015, ly = (l0 + l1) / 2,
         rx = .xrb - 0.015, ry = (r0 + r1) / 2, txt = sprintf("%.0f%%", pct))

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = .rib, aes(x, y, group = flow, fill = Stage),
               alpha = 0.55, color = NA) +
  geom_rect(data = .nd, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ntop, ymax = nbot,
                            fill = stage), color = NA) +
  geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(.nd, big),
            aes(x = tx, y = (ntop + nbot) / 2, label = lab, hjust = hj),
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.1, lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_text(data = dplyr::filter(.nd, !big),
            aes(x = tx, y = (ntop + nbot) / 2, label = lab, hjust = hj),
            color = "grey15", size = 2.8) +
  geom_text(data = .fll, aes(lx, ly, label = txt), hjust = 0, size = 2.9,
            color = "grey20") +
  geom_text(data = .fll, aes(rx, ry, label = txt), hjust = 1, size = 2.9,
            color = "grey20") +
  annotate("text", x = c((.xlb + .xle) / 2, (.xrb + .xre) / 2),
           y = -0.055 * max(.nd$nbot), fontface = "bold", size = 4.1,
           label = c("CKD-EPI creatinine", "CKD-EPI creatinine + cystatin C")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = .stage_pal, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_reverse(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.11, 0.04))) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.15, 1.15), expand = expansion(mult = 0.005)) +
  labs(title = "CKD stage: creatinine eGFR vs creatinine + cystatin C eGFR",
       subtitle = sprintf("Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 cohort, N = %d", nrow(stg)), x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

5 Fine-Gray Models — eGFR Difference as (CysC − Cr) / Cr, adjusted for CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (unindexed, mL/min) (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

These are the only two outcomes modelled on this page. Both run on the long-horizon kidney outcomes built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of Data Management: AKI is administratively censored at 365 days, the CKD composite runs to the last creatinine (day 0 → last follow-up). Death at any time is the competing event in both, taken from death_days_any rather than the 90-day death_90 flag, which cannot place a death in time beyond day 90. death_days_any is the union of the two sources that carry a death date — the RPDR Date_Of_Death when there is one, otherwise the REDCap last-follow-up date for a patient REDCap records as dead. Someone flagged deceased in RPDR with no date who is still alive in REDCap stays censored.

The exposure in both sections below is egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10 — 100 × (eGFR_CysC − eGFR_Cr) / eGFR_Cr, negated and divided by 10, so every subdistribution hazard ratio reads per 10 percentage-point decline. Cystatin C against creatinine alone, both unindexed. The two sections differ only in the kidney adjuster: creatinine eGFR in absolute mL/min here, indexed to body surface area in the next. All other adjusters are the project’s standard set (Section 1).

Each table shows univariable (one variable at a time) and multivariable Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard ratios side-by-side. A Word version of each table is saved during render — the download link sits under its heading.

Code 
.adj_set <- function(pre_labs, egfr_adj) {
  adj <- c("age","sex","score","ecog_score_cat2",
           "cancer_type_cat_7","high_dose",
           "Paclitaxel","Pemetrexed","Gemcitabine","ici",
           "bmi","smoking","thyroid")
  if (egfr_adj == "cockcroft") adj <- c(adj, "cockcroft")
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi")   adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys_unindex")
  # Indexed to BSA (mL/min/1.73m2), as opposed to the absolute mL/min above.
  if (egfr_adj == "ckd_epi_idx") adj <- c(adj, "ckd_epi_gfr_cre_cys")
  # Creatinine-only CKD-EPI 2021, race-free. Unlike the Cr-Cys forms above
  # it shares no measurement with the exposure.
  if (egfr_adj == "cre")     adj <- c(adj, "baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed")
  if (egfr_adj == "cre_idx") adj <- c(adj, "baseline_cre_egfr")
  if (!is.null(pre_labs)) adj <- c(adj, pre_labs)
  adj
}

# fg_model: returns univariable + multivariable merged Fine-Gray table.
# If docx_name is supplied, also saves the table as a .docx in docx_dir.
fg_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                     egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi", "ckd_epi_idx",
                                  "cre", "cre_idx"),
                     docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- tidycmprsk::crr(fmla_mv, failcode = 1, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = tidycmprsk::crr,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3),
      method.args = list(failcode = 1)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
fg_model <- .wrap_tbl(fg_model)


cox_model <- function(time_var, status_var, pred_var, pre_labs = NULL,
                      egfr_adj = c("none", "cockcroft", "ckd_epi", "ckd_epi_idx",
                                  "cre", "cre_idx"),
                      docx_name = NULL) {
  egfr_adj <- match.arg(egfr_adj)
  adj <- .adj_set(pre_labs, egfr_adj)
  all_vars <- c(pred_var, adj)

  fmla_mv <- as.formula(paste0(
    "Surv(", time_var, ", ", status_var, ") ~ ",
    paste(all_vars, collapse = " + ")
  ))
  tbl_mv <- survival::coxph(fmla_mv, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(exp = TRUE,
                   pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()

  y_call <- str2lang(sprintf("Surv(%s, %s)", time_var, status_var))
  tbl_uv <- rlang::inject(
    tbl_uvregression(
      data = dat,
      method = survival::coxph,
      y = !!y_call,
      include = dplyr::all_of(all_vars),
      exponentiate = TRUE,
      pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)
    )
  )

  out <- tbl_merge(
    tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
    tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**")
  )

  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
# Ritu: guard against unfittable sparse-outcome models.
cox_model <- .wrap_tbl(cox_model)

6 Fine-Gray Models — eGFR Difference as (CysC − Cr) / Cr, adjusted for CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine eGFR (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²) (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

Identical to the section above in every respect but one: the kidney adjuster is baseline_cre_egfr — CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine indexed to body surface area, mL/min/1.73m² — where the section above uses baseline_cre_egfr_unindexed, the same estimate in absolute mL/min.

Same exposure (egfr_diff_pct_sens_per10, per 10 percentage-point decline), same two outcomes, same competing event, same remaining covariates. The two sections therefore isolate what the BSA indexing of the adjuster does. The two forms correlate at 0.84, so they are related but not interchangeable.

Cockcroft-Gault is no longer an adjuster in either section.

7 Survivors Cohort — Follow-up > 365 Days (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

The Fine-Gray models above, rerun on patients still in follow-up beyond one year (days_last_follow_up > 365). Adjusted for baseline_cre_egfr (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²); same exposure and competing event, only the cohort changes.

This conditions on a post-baseline characteristic. Surviving and staying in follow-up past a year is partly a consequence of the kidney trajectory being modelled, so this subset is not a random sample and these estimates are not directly comparable with the full-cohort ones above. Read it as a restriction analysis, not a sensitivity analysis.

Code 
dat_full_cohort <- dat
dat <- dat_full_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

surv_counts <- tibble::tibble(

)

Code 
dat <- dat_full_cohort

8 Binary eGFR Difference (sens) — AKI and CKD Composite (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

The same two outcomes and the same adjusters as the Fine-Gray sections above, with the exposure entered as a binary split rather than per 10 percentage-point decline.

  • egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat splits at − 10 % — < -10% means the cystatin C eGFR sits more than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR; >= -10% is the reference.
  • egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20 splits at − 20 %, an intermediate cut.
  • egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30 splits at − 30 %, a smaller and more clearly discordant group.

Each subdistribution hazard ratio is therefore for the exposed group against its reference group, not per unit. Death at any time is the competing event and the kidney adjuster is baseline_cre_egfr (indexed, mL/min/1.73m²), as in the sections above.

8.1 Prevalence of the three cuts

Code 
.cut_row <- function(v, lab) tibble::tibble(
  Cut = lab, Exposed = sum(v), Unexposed = sum(!v),
  `% exposed` = round(100 * mean(v), 1),
  `AKI events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[v]  == 1),
  `AKI events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[!v] == 1),
  `CKD events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[v]  == 1),
  `CKD events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[!v] == 1))

cut_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat   == "< -10%", "< -10% (primary)"),
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20 == "< -20%", "< -20% (intermediate)"),
  .cut_row(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30 == "< -30%", "< -30% (stricter)"))

knitr::kable(cut_tbl, caption = sprintf(
  "Prevalence of the three binary cuts, N = %d. Median eGFR difference (sens) %.1f %%.",
  nrow(dat), median(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens, na.rm = TRUE)))

The six models above, repeated on the survivors cohort (days_last_follow_up > 365). Same exposures, outcomes, adjusters and competing event; only the cohort changes. As in the survivors section earlier, this conditions on a post-baseline characteristic, so these are a restriction analysis rather than a sensitivity check.

Code 
dat_full_cohort <- dat
dat <- dat_full_cohort %>%
  filter(!is.na(days_last_follow_up), days_last_follow_up > 365) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.factor) & !starts_with("cmp_status_"), droplevels))

binsurv <- purrr::map_dfr(
  list(c("< -10%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat"),
       c("< -20%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat20"),
       c("< -30%", "egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat30")),
  function(z) {
    e <- dat[[z[2]]] == z[1]
    tibble::tibble(Cut = z[1], `n survivors` = nrow(dat),
                   Exposed = sum(e), Unexposed = sum(!e),
                   `AKI events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[e]  == 1),
                   `AKI events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_aki_365[!e] == 1),
                   `CKD events, exposed`   = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[e]  == 1),
                   `CKD events, unexposed` = sum(dat$cmp_status_ckd_composite[!e] == 1))
  })
knitr::kable(binsurv, caption = sprintf(
  "Survivors cohort: %d of %d patients. Exposed-group event counts behind the six models below.",
  nrow(dat), nrow(dat_full_cohort)))

10 Paper

A total of 44 (31%) patients received an excess dose of carboplatin, defined as ≥ 25 mg higher than the dose that would have been predicted using the CKD-EPI eGFRCR-CYS equation adjusted for actual BSA.

(Denominator: 142 carboplatin AUC ≥ 3 patients with a computable predicted dose.)

11 365-Day Delta eGFR on the Binary eGFR Difference (sens) (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

The outcome is delta_egfr_d365 — eGFR at day 365 minus baseline, in mL/min/1.73m², negative = decline (see the Delta eGFR table above). Only patients with a creatinine within ± 45 days of day 365 contribute, so every model in this section is complete-case on that variable and its n is well below the cohort.

Both cuts of egfr_diff_pct_sens are reported: the primary one at − 10 % and the stricter one at − 30 %. < -10% means the cystatin C eGFR sits more than 10 % below the creatinine eGFR; >= -10% is the reference level.

11.1 365-day delta eGFR by group — cut at − 10 %

Code 
.grp_row <- function(d, lab) {
  v <- d$delta_egfr_d365[!is.na(d$delta_egfr_d365)]
  p <- d$delta_egfr_pct_d365[!is.na(d$delta_egfr_pct_d365)]
  tibble::tibble(
    Group = lab, n = length(v),
    `Delta eGFR, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(v), sd(v)),
    `Delta eGFR, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(v), quantile(v, .25), quantile(v, .75)),
    `Delta eGFR %, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
      median(p), quantile(p, .25), quantile(p, .75)))
}
d0 <- dat %>% filter(egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat == ">= -10%")
d1 <- dat %>% filter(egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat == "< -10%")
grp_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(.grp_row(d0, ">= -10% (reference)"), .grp_row(d1, "< -10%"))

.wt <- tryCatch(wilcox.test(delta_egfr_d365 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
.tt <- tryCatch(t.test(delta_egfr_d365 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
knitr::kable(grp_tbl, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "365-day delta eGFR by binary eGFR difference (sens). Negative = decline. ",
  "Wilcoxon p = %s; Welch t-test p = %s."),
  if (is.null(.wt)) "—" else format.pval(.wt$p.value, digits = 3),
  if (is.null(.tt)) "—" else format.pval(.tt$p.value, digits = 3)))
365-day delta eGFR by binary eGFR difference (sens). Negative = decline. Wilcoxon p = 0.247; Welch t-test p = 0.227.

11.2 Linear model — cut at − 10 %

Adjusted for the same multivariable covariate set as the Fine-Gray models, including the same kidney adjuster — baseline_cre_egfr, CKD-EPI 2021 race-free creatinine indexed to body surface area (mL/min/1.73m²). Coefficients are mL/min/1.73m² of 365-day eGFR change: a negative coefficient on < -10% means that group declined further.

📄 Download Word table

Code 
# .adj_set has three arguments on the whole/entire pages and two on the
# carboplatin pages; call it with whichever this page defines.
.adj_for <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj) {
  if (length(formals(.adj_set)) == 3) .adj_set(pred_var, NULL, egfr_adj)
  else .adj_set(NULL, egfr_adj)
}

lm_d365 <- function(pred_var, egfr_adj = "cre_idx", docx_name = NULL) {
  adj  <- .adj_for(pred_var, egfr_adj)
  vars <- c(pred_var, adj)
  fmla <- as.formula(paste("delta_egfr_d365 ~", paste(vars, collapse = " + ")))
  tbl_mv <- lm(fmla, data = dat) %>%
    tbl_regression(pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3)) %>%
    add_n()
  tbl_uv <- tbl_uvregression(
    data = dat %>% dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c("delta_egfr_d365", vars))),
    method = lm, y = delta_egfr_d365,
    pvalue_fun = function(x) style_pvalue(x, digits = 3))
  out <- tbl_merge(tbls = list(tbl_uv, tbl_mv),
                   tab_spanner = c("**Univariable**", "**Multivariable**"))
  if (!is.null(docx_name)) save_tbl_docx(out, docx_name)
  out
}
lm_d365 <- .wrap_tbl(lm_d365)

lm_d365("egfr_diff_pct_sens_cat", docx_name = "sec11_lm_d365")

12 Quartiles of eGFR Difference (sens) as the Exposure (Carboplatin AUC ≥ 3)

The same continuous exposure as the Fine-Gray sections above, entered as quartiles instead of a binary cut or a per-10-point slope. egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4 is built with dplyr::ntile(), so Q1 holds the most discordant quarter (cystatin C furthest below creatinine) and Q4 the least. Q4 is the reference level, so each ratio reads against the least discordant quarter and a value above 1 means more discordance carries more risk.

Same two outcomes, same competing event (death at any time), same multivariable set and the same kidney adjuster baseline_cre_egfr as everywhere else on this page. Three dummy terms replace one, so these models spend two more degrees of freedom than the binary ones on the same events.

12.1 Quartile boundaries and event counts

Code 
q_tbl <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4)) %>%
  group_by(Quartile = egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Range (%)` = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f",
                                  min(egfr_diff_pct_sens), max(egfr_diff_pct_sens)),
            `Median (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", median(egfr_diff_pct_sens)),
            `AKI events` = sum(cmp_status_aki_365 == 1),
            `CKD events` = sum(cmp_status_ckd_composite == 1),
            .groups = "drop")

knitr::kable(q_tbl, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "Quartiles of eGFR difference (sens), N = %d with a non-missing value. ",
  "Q4 (least discordant) is the reference level in every model below."),
  sum(!is.na(dat$egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4))))

12.6 365-Day Delta eGFR by Quartile

Code 
qd <- dat %>%
  filter(!is.na(egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4), !is.na(delta_egfr_d365)) %>%
  group_by(Quartile = egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Delta eGFR, mean (SD)` = sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)",
                                              mean(delta_egfr_d365), sd(delta_egfr_d365)),
            `Delta eGFR, median [IQR]` = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
              median(delta_egfr_d365), quantile(delta_egfr_d365, .25),
              quantile(delta_egfr_d365, .75)),
            .groups = "drop")

.kw <- tryCatch(kruskal.test(delta_egfr_d365 ~ egfr_diff_pct_sens_q4, data = dat),
                error = function(e) NULL)
knitr::kable(qd, caption = sprintf(paste0(
  "365-day delta eGFR by quartile of eGFR difference (sens). Negative = ",
  "decline. Kruskal-Wallis p = %s."),
  if (is.null(.kw)) "—" else format.pval(.kw$p.value, digits = 3)))
